Massive news out of the SEC 📣

They just proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, the SEC's first formal crypto rulemaking. 

It provides 2 paths for projects to sell tokens without registering with the SEC, plus a safe harbor.

 - Path one: a one-time raise of up to $5M over a four-year period, no registration required.
- Path two: up to $75M in any 12-month period (with financials and some ongoing reporting)

With the new safe harbor, a qualifying token stops being subject to securities rules once the issuer completes the essential managerial efforts it promised.

The rules would also preempt state securities laws.

This substantially opens the door for ICOs in the US...

BREAKING: US margin debt dropped -$85 billion in July, to $1.42 trillion, the largest monthly decline on record.

This also marks the first monthly decrease since March.

By comparison, the 2nd-biggest monthly drop was recorded in January 2022 at -$80 billion, just as the bear market started.

This all follows a +$198 billion jump in margin debt in May and June, the largest 2-month increase on record.

Despite this record decline, margin debt has still surged +$518 billion, or +58%, since the start of 2025.

Levered investors were crushed last month.

BREAKING: Hedge funds purchased US equities in every trading session last week.

In total, this marked their 2nd-largest weekly purchase over the last 12 months.

Single stocks accounted for ~70% of the total, driven primarily by long equity purchases and, to a lesser extent, short covering.

Information technology and communication services saw the strongest demand, with 8 of 11 sectors recording purchases.

Meanwhile, macro products, such as index futures and ETFs, accounted for ~30% of total demand, with short positions in US-listed ETFs reduced for the 6th consecutive week.

Hedge funds are doubling down on US equities.

tweets.text:
Some thoughts on PA Gov. Shapiro executive order on data centers -->

1) The State had a mechanism for expedited data center approvals. That is gone.

2) Developers need local approval before the state will issue a permit. DEP will still review in parallel, but nothing gets granted until local land use approvals are in hand. Previously the state process could get a head start and finish first.

3) New DCs now have to pay the full cost of the power and grid infrastructure they require, while meeting new water, labor and community requirements

4) State agencies can no longer sign NDAs.

All of these seem broadly consistent with where Shapiro was already heading. This move is not as aggressive as Texas or New York, in the sense that there is no freeze on new energizations here. Still, adds another layer of uncertainty ahead of the election, especially with a Republican challenger who seems even MORE anti-DCs than Dem incumbent Shapiro.

For $KEEL, my thoughts:
>Sharon (110MW) unaffected (ready for service end-2027). City council already approved final land development plans. Water use was already conditioned out at zoning (no river withdrawal), and the site is grandfathered under Mercer County's new ordinance. Environmental permits are all that's left.
>Panther Creek (350MW): delivery capacity and the interconnect are secured with PPL, and KEEL is funding the new line entirely (already the EO's standard). Two items outstanding: final land development approval from the town (pending) and then the DEP environmental permits. So now they need the town approval first. Key hearing this Thursday on the local stormwater permit.
>Scrubgrass, longer-dated project not in the stock: KEEL has BYOP plans for this site which is in line with Governor's EO, but hard to think this doesn't slip from 2028+.
